necessity.derivation_is_independent_of_any_impleme: The necessity below is derived ENTIRELY from (a) the frozen stella_0001_successor_contract in P1A_FULL_BOOTSTRAP_AUTHORITY_v1.0.0.json and (b) the state of the two files at BASE_SHA. No implementation diff, commit or pull request is cited as its basis. The counterfactual measurement recorded afterwards is CORROBORATION of a conclusion already reached from frozen text, never its source.
necessity.step_1_frozen_contract: P1A_FULL_BOOTSTRAP_AUTHORITY_v1.0.0.json stella_0001_successor_contract.authorized_change, verbatim: 'ONLY the conversion of the two already-existing canonical grants — CREATE ON SCHEMA public (line 176) and USAGE ON SCHEMA auth (line 181) — from grant-producing behaviour into ASSERTIONS that db/prepared/stella_local_0000_local_role_identity_bootstrap.sql already established them.' assertion_semantics adds that the assertions must FAIL CLOSED and must 'never re-grant as a fallback'.
necessity.step_2_base_state_of_the_sql: MEASURED at BASE_SHA — db/prepared/stella_0001_role_topology_bootstrap.sql:181 is exactly `GRANT USAGE ON SCHEMA auth TO uellix_owner;`, and :176 is `GRANT CREATE ON SCHEMA public TO uellix_owner;`. These are the two statements the contract names, at the line numbers it names.
necessity.step_3_base_state_of_the_test: MEASURED at BASE_SHA — tests/database-role-safety.test.ts:278 declares `it('grants exactly one schema-level privilege outside public, and it is USAGE on auth', ...)`. It scans the stella_0001 source with the regex /\b(GRANT|REVOKE)\s+[A-Z, ]+\s+ON\s+SCHEMA\s+(\w+)[^;]*;/gi, filters out schema public, and then asserts at :284 `expect(outsidePublic).toHaveLength(1)` and at :285 that the survivor matches /GRANT\s+USAGE\s+ON\s+SCHEMA\s+auth\s+TO\s+uellix_owner/i.
necessity.step_4_deterministic_consequence: The regex matches only GRANT/REVOKE statements. A fail-closed has_schema_privilege() assertion is neither. Therefore ANY implementation conforming to the frozen successor contract removes the sole non-public match, `outsidePublic` becomes length 0, and the assertion at :284 fails deterministically. The test's expectation is a HISTORICAL expectation that the authorized conversion makes false by construction. This conclusion follows from steps 1-3 alone.

counterfactual_measurement.conclusion: Reverting this one test while keeping the authorized implementation makes CI fail deterministically on a false historical expectation, and no other control is disturbed. The delta is therefore MECHANICALLY REQUIRED, minimal, and confined to one assertion.
counterfactual_measurement.reversion_proof: Both files were restored to their BASE_SHA blobs and the working tree verified clean before this artifact was written.
